title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use urgent language to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or Medicare number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts with Dangerous Links
how_it_works: You get a text message saying you have a package waiting, with a link to track it. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or puts a virus on your phone.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your details here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don't recognize
Requests for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Do not click the link—delete the message and contact the delivery company using their official website if you’re expecting a package.

title: Social Security Email Phishing Scam
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they’re from the Social Security Administration, asking you to click a link to fix a problem with your account. The link goes to a fake website that steals your information.
example_message: "We noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Click here to review your information."
red_flags: Email asks you to click a link or download an attachment
what_to_do: Do not click any links—go to the official Social Security website or call them directly if you’re concerned.

title: Facebook 'Friend in Need' Money Request
how_it_works: A scammer hacks your friend's Facebook account and sends you a message saying they need money for an emergency. They ask you to send money quickly, often using gift cards or wire transfers.
example_message: "Hi, I’m in trouble and need your help. Can you send me $200 in gift cards right away?"
red_flags: Urgent request for money from a friend
Asked to send gift cards or wire money
Message seems out of character for your friend
what_to_do: Call your friend directly using their real phone number to check if the request is real.

title: Tech Support Pop-Up Scam
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a phone number for help. If you call, the scammer may ask for money or remote access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up uses scary warnings about viruses
Tells you to call a phone number right away
Asks for payment or remote access to your computer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number—run a trusted antivirus scan or ask a family member for help.
